requirements.summary: Run-mode policy must preserve unresolved DAE specifics as distinct tracked items, including jail durability, yolo guard ambiguity, and external_publish_side_effect handling.

decisions.summary: blocked_sequence is runtime scheduler/executor owned, monotonic per run/node, starts at 1, and increments only for new blocked episodes.
decisions.raw_excerpt: `blocked_sequence` should be owned by the runtime scheduler/executor layer... monotonic per `{ run_id, node_id }` ... starts at `1` ... increments only when the node transitions from non-blocked to a new blocked episode.
decisions.decision_rationale: Ownership ambiguity was identified as the seam; naming was already stable.

decisions.summary: request_id is subordinate compatibility metadata mapped 1:1 to blocked episode identity and must not be the only durable key.
decisions.raw_excerpt: `blocked_sequence` should be canonical; `request_id` should become a child/compatibility handle... `request_id` maps 1:1 to `{ run_id, node_id, blocked_sequence }` ... must never be the only durable key.
decisions.decision_rationale: Preserves UI/history compatibility while preventing recovery-key ambiguity.

decisions.summary: Startup recovery must rehydrate unresolved blocked episodes and emit startup_recovered without reminting blocked episodes.
decisions.raw_excerpt: On restart, the runtime restores current unresolved blocked episodes... emits a scheduler pass with `wake_reason = startup_recovered` ... does not mint new blocked episodes by itself.
decisions.decision_rationale: Avoids silent block-loss and accidental blocked-sequence churn.

decisions.summary: A canonical execution_unit_context should replace TierContext as runtime truth, with decomposition_context retained only as derived selection/view helper.
decisions.raw_excerpt: Canonical object: `execution_unit_context` ... Optional derived object: `decomposition_context` or `selection_context`
decisions.decision_rationale: Owner split is explicit; mixed TierContext duplicates and blurs runtime identity ownership.

decisions.summary: execution_role belongs in canonical attempt/dispatch packets while operational_identity belongs in receipt/side-effect bridge families.
decisions.raw_excerpt: `execution_role` belongs in the canonical runtime attempt/dispatch packet family... `operational_identity` belongs in the operational bridge family...
decisions.decision_rationale: Separates actor-role semantics from external target semantics to prevent identity-field overloading.
